NVDA – Balance sheet disclosure is the key catalyst 
FQ2 should deliver the usual 3–4% sales beat and raise on the Vera Rubin ramp, but 
earnings are not the main debate. The key is whether NVDA provides greater disclosure on its 
multi-year commitments to secure supply, power, cloud capacity, models and demand. Since 
announcing its US$100bn OpenAI investment, NVDA’s forward EV/EBITDA has de-rated 44% 
from around 27x to 15x, less than half AMD’s 32x. This appears excessive versus the estimated 
worst-case US$500bn funding burden, equivalent to only around 10% of NVDA’s EV. If AI 
demand remains resilient, much of this contingent burden may never materialize. A larger 
buyback could become the next re-rating catalyst. NVDA currently returns only around 37% 
of FCF, versus Apple’s historical 82%. With NVDA potentially generating nearly US$1bn of daily 
FCF by next year, raising the payout to 50–75% would still leave sufficient capacity to support 
its ecosystem while placing a floor under the share price. 
 
****Sales View: The earnings beat is largely priced in, but better balance-sheet disclosure 
and a larger buyback are not. These catalysts could ease concerns over AI overinvestment 
and drive a re-rating from the current depressed multiple. Also watch growth from AI cloud, 
industrial, enterprise and sovereign customers, which could diversify NVDA away from 
hyperscalers developing competing custom chips.
